```suggestion
  opts.etag ??= this.app.enabled('etag');
```

This would slightly change logic (overwrite `undefined` **and `null`**), but why not write it the easier way (boolean is expected anyway). Nullish coalescing assignment was [designed for such use case](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-logical-assignment#motivation).
Done in 16671ee: switched to `??=` and put the comment back to the original one-liner. As you noted, an explicit `etag: null` now falls back to the app setting as well.

`String(url)` fixes the `TypeError` for `URL` instances, but it also silently converts `null`, `undefined`, and arbitrary objects into the literal header values `Location: null`, `Location: undefined`, and `Location: [object Object]`. Before this change those inputs threw at `loc.toLowerCase()`, which made the caller's bug visible instead of shipping a bogus redirect target. Consider coercing more deliberately, e.g. accept strings as-is, call `.toString()`/`String()` only for `URL`-like objects (`url instanceof URL` or duck-typing `href`), and keep throwing (or add an explicit `TypeError` with a clear message) for `null`/`undefined`.
It would make sense to split the `null` case from the `boolean | number` case to avoid using a ternary.
Do not pass in non-booleans to the sub module, because that is just asking for undefined behavior later. The etag option only accepts true or false.
